recentItems.title: Why do people hide chronic illness at work? | Alyssa McGonagle | TEDxUNCCharlotte
recentItems.description:
Chronic conditions are something that effects a large portion of the population. Despite this, workplaces are not designed to support individuals with chronic conditions. It is important to reimagine the workplace and identify specific strategies employers can use to support employees with chronic conditions better.

Alyssa McGonagle is an Associate Professor of Psychological and Organizational Science at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte. Alyssa has been studying the challenges that workers and organizations face around chronic health conditions, and how to address them, for the last 15 years. Alyssa recently published a book on the topic titled, “Chronic Health Conditions and Work: Proactive Strategies for Supporting Employees and Doing Well by Doing Good." 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: From Undocumented to Unprecedented | Tsion Michael | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
At seventeen years old, top of her class, prom queen, and dreaming of the Ivy League — Tsion Michael walked into her guidance counselor's office and was told five words that were supposed to end her story:

"Your future is illegal."

What followed was a decade in the shadows. No college financial aid. No legal path forward. No certainty about tomorrow. Tsion was undocumented — not because her family had done anything wrong, but because her father, a multilingual CPA and strategic leader, made the courageous choice to go all in for the liberation of his people in Eritrea. That sacrifice triggered a legal consequence none of them saw coming.

In this riveting, deeply personal TEDx talk, Tsion introduces the concept of the Rented Identity — the suffocating experience of performing a restricted version of yourself that does not technically belong to you.  She traces her decade-long fight from the shadows to citizenship. And she reveals the unexpected truth she found on the other side: the very season that was meant to erase her was actually forming her.

Today, Tsion is an HR executive, author, doctoral candidate, and co-founder of Arise and Shine Global — a 501(c)(3) nonprofit championing immigrants, refugees, and marginalized communities worldwide. Her mission is clear: no one should ever be told their potential has an expiration date.

There is a superpower hidden in every wound that did not destroy you.

This talk will help you find yours. Tsion Michael is a TEDx speaker, HR executive, author, and global advocate whose story begins with five words that were supposed to end it: "Your future is illegal."
A former undocumented immigrant who spent a decade in the shadows, Tsion went on to build a 20-year career in finance and human resources leadership across 40+ countries, earning an MBA from Liberty University, a Labor and Employment Law degree from Tulane University Law school, and is currently a Doctoral Candidate at Liberty University. 

She is the founder of Inspire Every Life LLC, a consulting firm, and the host of the Inspire Every Life podcast — a personal development and leadership show focused on discovering one's purpose, alignment, and breaking free from fear and mediocrity.

Driven by her own immigration journey, Tsion co-founded Arise and Shine Global alongside her father — the same man whose courageous sacrifice for the Eritrean liberation movement set her story in motion. The foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to championing vulnerable populations through housing, education, resources, and advocacy.

She is the author of The Aligned Woman: Is It Well With Your Soul? and the forthcoming Inspire Every Life: A Journey to Transformation and Unleashing the Power Within.
Tsion speaks, consults, and leads from one unshakeable conviction: the world does not need the rented version of you. It needs the real one. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Single Mother by Choice | Krysta Monet | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
What happens if you're never chosen?

From an early age, many women are taught that life begins after someone chooses them, a partner, an employer, an opportunity. We learn to wait for permission, validation, and the "right time" before building the lives we truly want.

In this TEDx talk, Krysta Monet explores what happens if that moment never comes and why waiting to be chosen may be one of the greatest limitations we place on ourselves. 

Through her deeply personal decision to become a single mother by choice, she challenges the belief that a meaningful life must follow a traditional timeline and offers a new perspective on agency, courage, and creating a life on your own terms.

This isn't a talk about motherhood. It's about identity, possibility, and the quiet revolution that begins when we stop asking, "Who will choose me?" and start asking, "What will I choose for myself?" Krysta Monet is a writer, speaker, and cultural commentator exploring the complexities of modern womanhood. Through essays, conversations, and live experiences, she examines the invisible rules women inherit about love, ambition, identity, loneliness, and the courage to choose lives that feel true instead of simply expected. Her work invites women to question cultural narratives and create lives on their own terms. She has been featured in media outlets such as Cosmopolitan and FOX26. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Figure-It-Out-ness: What to Do When You Don’t Know What to Do | David Settle | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
What do the world’s greatest innovators, entrepreneurs, and everyday problem-solvers have in common? They all faced moments where they had no idea what to do next.

In this inspiring and practical TEDx talk, David Settle introduces the concept of “Figure-It-Out-ness”—the often-overlooked skill of navigating uncertainty with curiosity, resilience, and action. Drawing from his experiences as an entrepreneur, educator, celebrity photographer, and tech startup founder, David challenges the belief that success comes from always having the right answers. Instead, he reveals how embracing the words “I don’t know” can become the catalyst for innovation, growth, and breakthrough.

Blending personal stories, humor, and actionable insights, this talk equips audiences with a framework for tackling life’s biggest challenges when the path forward isn’t obvious. Whether you’re building a business, leading a team, pursuing a dream, or simply facing an uncertain future, you’ll leave with the confidence to stop fearing the unknown—and start figuring it out. David Settle is a celebrity photographer, entrepreneur, author, and tech startup founder dedicated to helping people and businesses turn ideas into impact. With more than two decades of experience spanning media, education, and entrepreneurship, he has worked with some of the biggest names in entertainment while building brands that blend creativity with innovation. As the co-founder of Moonlight, an on-demand marketplace transforming the photography and videography industry, David is passionate about using technology to solve real-world problems. A TEDx speaker, educator, and storyteller, he inspires audiences to embrace uncertainty, cultivate resilience, and develop the “figure-it-out” mindset that fuels breakthrough success. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: No Such Thing as 'Fast' | Alexus Grace Rhone | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
In "No Such Thing as 'Fast'," Alexus Grace (Rhone) examines how flawed social science research became cultural shorthand that mischaracterized Black girls as “fast” and families as “broken.” Tracing these labels from academic studies to everyday language, she reveals how data without context can harden into identity—shaping not only perception, but lived experience.

Blending personal narrative, cultural analysis, and storytelling practice, Alexus introduces “re-storying” as a corrective approach—one that restores complexity, dignity, and agency to lives flattened by oversimplified conclusions. She challenges the assumption that research is neutral, reframing it instead as a powerful narrative force that must be handled with care.

Ultimately, this talk expands beyond one community to ask a universal question: What happens when people are defined before they are fully formed? In an era where more people than ever have the tools to shape stories, Alexus invites us to take responsibility for how we name, frame, and carry one another’s lives—recognizing that there is no such thing as “fast,” only human beings in the ongoing process of becoming. Alexus Grace (Rhone) is a writer, producer, and artistic theologian devoted to exploring the power of truth when ‘dressed’ in story.

Founder of Truth Meet Story, Alexus tells stories about the sweetness of Black girls and the compassion of Black women on diverse platforms - on page, stage, screen, web, radio, and podcasts.

She entered the creative ecosystem publishing a YA novel series targeting reluctant readers. Premature Pleasures, Secret Shame, Backseats and Bleachers: A High School Love Story, and Cover The Coo are page-turning “mirrors” and love notes to her readers.

Over the past 25 years, she expanded her storytelling repertoire to include stage productions “Call & Response,” “Ancient Of Ways: For Colored Girls Who’ve Considered Ifa When Jesus Came Up Short,” “Pitching My Tent Too Close To Sodom: Justice For Rosa Lee Ingram”; digital storytelling series’ “#TheBounceBackRDU,” “#Proverbs32,” and award-winning documentary “Religion, Philosophy & Mental Health in Black Americans.”

Deeply impacted by the creative journey of Alice Childress, Alexus writes, directs, and produces original content for this context. The burden of this moment in history to counter the attempts to erase Black women’s contributions and Black girls’ value undergirds the framing and tone of her narratives.

She holds a Master of Arts in Theology from Fuller Theological Seminary in Pasadena, California, and a Bachelor of Journalism from the University of Texas at Austin. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why AI Will End the Attention Economy | Christopher Loo | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
For years, we've lived in an attention economy where followers, likes, and virality determined who was seen, trusted, and rewarded. But artificial intelligence is quietly changing the rules.

In this thought-provoking talk, physician-turned-entrepreneur Dr. Christopher H. Loo, MD-PhD argues that we're entering an era where authority—not attention—will become the most valuable currency. As AI-powered search and answer engines increasingly determine what information people discover and trust, long-term credibility, evidence, and a body of work matter more than ever.

Drawing from his own journey of leaving medicine during the 2008 financial crisis, rebuilding his career through media and technology, and hosting more than 1,500 podcast conversations, Dr. Loo reveals why the future belongs to those who build trust instead of chasing trends.

If AI is rewriting the rules of influence, trust, and opportunity, what should we be building instead? Dr. Christopher H. Loo, MD-PhD, is a physician, entrepreneur, investor, and speaker whose work explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping authority, trust, and financial opportunity.

After leaving medicine during the 2008 financial crisis, he achieved financial independence through strategic investing before reinventing himself again by building a top 5% globally ranked podcast into a six-figure media brand. Today, through more than 1,500 interviews with entrepreneurs, executives, and innovators, he examines what it takes to remain relevant in a world where AI is transforming how we discover expertise and build influence.

A graduate of Rice University and Baylor College of Medicine, Dr. Loo believes the future belongs not to those who chase attention, but to those who build enduring authority. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Coffee with Wilma Flintstone | Gail Awan PhD | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
What if the most important map you’ll ever explore isn’t the world—but yourself?

In this thought-provoking talk, Dr. Gail Awan introduces J.O.G.I.™ (Journey • Origin • Geography • Identity), a framework that explores how history, ancestry, geography, and personal experience shape the stories we tell about ourselves and others. Drawing from science, history, culture, and storytelling, she challenges audiences to see identity as something richer than labels or DNA alone.

Through an unexpected conversation with Wilma Flintstone, Dr. Awan invites us to ask a timeless question: What kind of ancestor will you become? The result is a fresh perspective on empathy, belonging, and the legacy each of us has the power to create. Dr. Gail Awan is a nonprofit executive, cultural storyteller, author, and two-time TEDx speaker with more than 25 years of experience leading community-based initiatives. She is the creator of J.O.G.I.™ (Journey • Origin • Geography • Identity), a storytelling framework that invites people to explore how history, ancestry, geography, and identity shape who they are—and to consider what kind of ancestors they will become. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Stitched is not healed | Elena Sarango-Muniz | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
What if your greatest strength isn't something you built but something you survived? In this talk, Elena Sarango-Muniz challenges the way we think about professional excellence. After 25 years in HR, she discovered that the qualities making leaders exceptional often trace back to childhood wounds... to old verdicts we've spent our careers trying to overturn. Your perfectionism, your caretaking, your relentless drive, they all have a story. But here's the paradox: stitched wounds are not the same as healed wounds. Learning to live with what shaped us isn't weakness. It's wisdom.
 
This talk is for anyone who's ever wondered why they work so hard, who they're really trying to prove something to, and what might change if they stopped trying to erase their wounds and started learning from them instead. Elena Sarango-Muniz is an executive coach and former HR leader with 25 years in global corporate environments. She works with senior leaders to uncover how their greatest professional strengths often began as old wounds they've spent careers trying to overturn. A Peruvian immigrant, Elena brings a mentor's warmth and a storyteller's eye to the work of emotional intelligence. She believes our scars tell us who we are. The question is whether we're still bleeding into them. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Quite Extrovert Advantage: Say Less, Become M.O.R.E. | Michelle Gines | TEDxThird Ward Salon
recentItems.description:
For generations, we've celebrated the loudest voices as the strongest leaders. We've been taught that confidence looks like speaking first, speaking often, and commanding every room we enter.

But what if we've been measuring influence all wrong?

In this talk, Michelle Gines introduces the concept of the Quiet Extrovert, someone who is energized by people yet leads through observation, intentionality, and meaningful connection rather than constant visibility. Drawing from her own experiences in leadership, publishing, and personal transformation, she shares how quiet influence often creates deeper trust, stronger relationships, and more sustainable impact than attention alone.

Using her M.O.R.E. Framework, Michelle offers a practical approach for recognizing and embracing a leadership style that has too often been overlooked. Rather than encouraging people to become someone they're not, she invites them to become more fully themselves.

This talk challenges the belief that influence belongs only to the loudest voices and offers a compelling alternative: authentic leadership built on clarity, presence, and purposeful action. Michelle Gines is a leadership strategist, publisher, and thought leader dedicated to helping accomplished professionals transform their expertise into lasting authority and meaningful impact. Throughout her career, she has worked alongside executives, entrepreneurs, healthcare leaders, ministry leaders, and authors, helping them uncover the wisdom within their experiences and communicate it with clarity and purpose.

As the founder of Purpose Publishing, Michelle has guided the publication of hundreds of books and has witnessed firsthand that the greatest value people possess often remains hidden beneath years of experience. This realization shaped her belief that true leadership is not about becoming louder but about becoming more intentional.

Her work now centers on helping individuals recognize their unique influence, build trusted authority, and create legacies that extend beyond titles or accomplishments. Through speaking, coaching, publishing, and strategic consulting, Michelle encourages others to lead with authenticity, quiet confidence, and purpose. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: O porão | Sônia Bossolani | TEDxAraraquara
recentItems.description: O que guardamos nos porões que existem dentro de nós? Sônia Bossolani usa essa metáfora para falar sobre lembranças dolorosas, ressentimentos e sentimentos que tentamos esconder, mas que continuam influenciando nossa vida. Ao compartilhar a perda de uma sobrinha em um acidente e o longo processo de elaborar o luto, ela revela como encontrou, atrás da dor, uma culpa que ainda precisava ser compreendida. Um relato íntimo sobre a coragem de iluminar nossas feridas, rever julgamentos e reconhecer a humanidade em nós e nos outros — abrindo espaço para o perdão, a libertação e a paz. Sônia Bossolani é gestora social e atua há décadas no desenvolvimento de projetos voltados ao acolhimento e à proteção de crianças, adolescentes e famílias em situação de vulnerabilidade. Ao longo de sua trajetória, construiu uma carreira marcada pelo compromisso com o cuidado, a escuta e a promoção da dignidade humana. Sua experiência profissional a colocou em contato com histórias de superação, resiliência e transformação que reforçam diariamente o valor dos vínculos humanos. A partir de vivências pessoais profundas, Sônia também passou a refletir sobre a importância de reconhecer e compreender os momentos mais difíceis da vida como parte fundamental do processo de crescimento e autoconhecimento. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
